No mismatch, and no other instrument in the battery has 6 items on 1-7. (2) TEXT SOURCE. The OSF deposit (osf.io/45aq3) holds only PsyR_lockdown2020.R and data.PsyR_lockdown2020.csv; the CSV is a bare header row (GQ_1..GQ_6 among Hope_*, Opt_*, Cog_*, ...) with no variable or value labels, and the .R is an lme4/lmerTest analysis script containing no item strings. The Frontiers article has no supplementary material and reproduces only the two example items above. So the wording ships from the instrument's own published form: McCullough, Emmons & Tsang (2002) 'The grateful disposition', J Pers Soc Psychol 82(1):112-127, Appendix A, as distributed in full by the first author at pages.ucsd.edu/~memccullough/gratitude/GQ-6-scoring-interp.pdf, transcribed verbatim including terminal periods. One deliberate normalisation: the source PDF renders item 3 with a typographic apostrophe ('don’t'); the shipped string uses the ASCII apostrophe. Item 5 is shipped as the author's own form has it, 'more able to appreciate'; note that some validation papers (e.g. the Chilean one, PMC4815209) reprint it as 'better able to appreciate'. (3) LANGUAGE / FALLBACK. The study administered the French GQ-6 of Shankland & Martin-Krumm (2012, Pratiques Psychologiques 18(2):171-187) to a French sample. That French wording is NOT recoverable in scope: it is in neither the OSF deposit (both files checked; no French item text, only codes) nor the paper or its supplements (there are none). So the documented fallback applies - English in the base fields, the _translated columns omitted entirely, language='French', text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english (McCullough et al.'s own English for the same numbered items). No machine translation was produced. Shankland & Martin-Krumm is a paywalled Elsevier article and was not consulted; recovering the administered French is a later backfill, not part of this pass. (4) OPTIONS. All seven points carry a label because the instrument's own published form labels all seven (1 = strongly disagree, 2 = disagree, 3 = slightly disagree, 4 = neutral, 5 = slightly agree, 6 = agree, 7 = strongly agree). CAVEAT, disclosed in the public_note: the study prints only its two endpoints (1 = 'strongly disagree' to 7 = 'strongly agree', which match the instrument's), so the five intermediate labels are the instrument's, not evidence about what the French form showed. Nothing was padded with its own number. Direction confirmed against the data: the four positively worded items sit at 4.90-5.54 of 7 and the two negatively worded ones at 3.19 and 3.38, and reverse-keying items 3 and 6 lifts raw alpha from 0.14 to 0.81 - consistent with 7 = agree, not the reverse. (5) INSTRUCTIONS deliberately blank. The study publishes none, and the instrument's own instruction ('Using the scale below as a guide, write a number beside each statement...') describes a paper-and-pencil administration that this online survey did not use, so shipping it would have been a false claim about what respondents read. correct_response blank (attitude scale, no key). section_id is the trivial single value with no section_prompt. (6) MAPPING. mapping_basis=paper_order, Step 5b status PARTIAL. The IRW codes ARE the deposit's column names (code-derivation pattern 1), but the deposit has no labels, so the tie GQ_k <-> GQ-6 item k is a number-to-number order inference that nothing states. Two checks constrain it, both in verify_pellerin2020_gq6.R: (A) the deposit's own derived Grat.world column is reproduced to 3.6e-15 by the 6-item mean with exactly columns 3 and 6 reversed, and by none of the other 63 reversal subsets (next-best deviation 1.17), which fixes {GQ_3,GQ_6} as the reverse pair - and the canonical GQ-6's reverse pair is items 3 and 6, sitting at exactly those positions; (B) on the live table GQ_3 and GQ_6 are the only two items with a negative mean correlation to the rest, GQ_6 has by far the weakest keyed loading (0.436 vs 0.650-0.875), matching item 6's documented status as the GQ-6's weak item (loading .079 in the Chilean adult EFA, PMC4815209 Table 1; 0.29 in the German validation, PMC7586006; .52 in the Brazilian one - it is the item dropped to form the GQ-5), and GQ_1/GQ_2 are the two strongest (0.850/0.875), matching items 1 and 2 as the near-synonymous top-loading pair (.838/.812). WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: GQ_1 vs GQ_2 and GQ_4 vs GQ_5. Both checks act on blocks, and no published per-item statistic orders those pairs reproducibly - the Chilean EFA puts item 5 (.749) above item 4 (.701) while the live data puts them the other way round (0.650 vs 0.742), and the 'As I get older' item shows no age gradient here to mark it (partial r with age, controlling the scale total, is +0.022 for GQ_5 against +0.026 for GQ_2). Those two within-block orderings rest on the columns being numbered in the instrument's own order, which every checkable point is consistent with and none contradicts. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.
